propositions: Expected lost-contention push failures and transient transport retries are surfaced at WARNING to agent-visible stderr with wording that primes LLM sessions to investigate non-issues, causing agents to halt and waste tokens on non-actionable diagnostics.
Mid-retry transient transport notices and the unpushed-backlog suffix (especially bare `..HEAD` wording) escalate false urgency across concurrent sessions without stating the self-healing contract.

Expected and auto-handled push failures must be demoted from WARNING/INFO to DEBUG and removed from agent-visible output under normal concurrent-writer load, reserving WARNING only for genuine operator-actionable signals: policy declines, strict-mode failures, and proven-growing backlogs.

The `unpushed_summary` message must name the tickets branch explicitly (not bare `..HEAD`), state the self-healing contract (committed locally, publish on next successful push), and avoid bare-HEAD misinterpretation across sessions.

The backlog count escalation must be compared against the prior push-pending marker to detect PROVEN growth before escalating to WARNING; a static or non-zero count alone is not an outage signal under normal load.
